html: Noise does not touch the vessel. There is no particle, no receptor for sound in the aorta, and the sound pressure that matters is far below what damages the ear: in the mouse model behind this module the mean level is 72 dB(A) with peaks of 85 dB(A), and white noise of the same mean level leaves the vasculature untouched. What reaches the vessel is the stress response the pattern of the sound provokes, and this module draws it as three hormones arriving in the plasma, catecholamines from the sympathetic arm, angiotensin II from the renin-angiotensin system it drives, and cortisol from the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal arm. From there the mechanism is chemistry. Angiotensin II through its AT1 receptor drives the phagocyte-type NADPH oxidase, and the superoxide it makes is where the module hands over to the rest of the atlas; that this oxidase is the decisive one is not an inference, since mice without NOX2 keep their endothelial function under noise, and removing the lysozyme M-positive myeloid cells that carry most of it into the vessel wall has the same effect. The second half of the module is the switch inside the endothelial cell, and it is the part that makes noise look like every other cardiovascular risk factor. The synthase that should relax the vessel is not switched off: noise raises both its protein and its activating phosphorylation at Ser1177. It is turned round. Two modifications do it, and the map draws both. Oxidised glutathione S-glutathionylates two cysteines of the reductase domain, a reversible mark that is raised in the aorta and the heart at every day of exposure, and peroxynitrite, made when the nitric oxide that is still produced meets the superoxide, oxidises the tetrahydrobiopterin the enzyme needs as a cofactor to its radical. Either way the enzyme passes its electrons to oxygen instead of to arginine and becomes a second superoxide source, which is why inhibiting it in a noise-exposed vessel lowers superoxide instead of raising it. The two outputs follow. The cyclase route runs dry, and the phosphorylation of VASP at Ser239, the readout that follows vascular nitric oxide most closely, falls even though the cyclase itself is unchanged; and the endothelium makes more endothelin-1, which leaves the cell as a constrictor. Both are drawn to the edge of this module and no further: the relaxation and the constriction themselves belong to the smooth muscle layer, which is a tissue module of its own.
